mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the formation of a covalent bond by orbital overlap is NOT true?

options.A: Overlap of two half‑filled orbitals leads to a sigma bond.
options.B: Overlap of a filled orbital with an empty orbital can form a covalent bond.
options.C: Maximum bond strength is obtained when the overlapping orbitals have the same shape and orientation.
options.D: Orbital overlap can occur only between atoms of the same element.

mcqs.answer: Orbital overlap can occur only between atoms of the same element.
mcqs.explanation: Covalent bonds are formed by the overlap of atomic orbitals from any two atoms, regardless of whether they belong to the same element. Statements A, B and C correctly describe aspects of orbital overlap; statement D is a misconception and therefore the correct answer.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a sigma (σ) bond from a pi (π) bond?

options.A: A sigma bond is formed by head‑on (end‑to‑end) overlap of orbitals, giving the greatest overlap.
options.B: A pi bond is formed by head‑on overlap of orbitals, giving the greatest overlap.
options.C: A sigma bond involves side‑by‑side overlap of two p orbitals only.
options.D: A pi bond is always stronger than a sigma bond because it involves d‑orbital overlap.

mcqs.answer: A sigma bond is formed by head‑on (end‑to‑end) overlap of orbitals, giving the greatest overlap.
mcqs.explanation: Sigma bonds arise from head‑on (axial) overlap of orbitals (s‑s, s‑p, or p‑p), which provides the maximum orbital overlap and therefore a stronger bond. Pi bonds result from side‑by‑side (lateral) overlap of parallel p orbitals and are generally weaker. Options B, C and D describe pi bonds incorrectly.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate hybrid orbitals to molecular geometry
mcqs.question: Which pair correctly matches the type of hybridization of the central atom with its observed molecular geometry (considering only sigma bonds)?
mcqs.explanation: sp² hybridization mixes one s and two p orbitals, producing three equivalent sp² hybrids that arrange themselves in a trigonal planar geometry with 120° bond angles. sp hybridization gives linear geometry, sp³ gives tetrahedral, and sp³d gives trigonal bipyramidal, so the other options are incorrect.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand limitations of simple valence-bond description
mcqs.question: Which observation cannot be adequately explained by the simple valence‑bond model that considers only sigma and pi overlap?

options.A: The bond length of O₂ is shorter than the sum of the covalent radii of two oxygen atoms.

mcqs.explanation: The simple valence‑bond picture predicts that all electrons in O₂ are paired, which would make the molecule diamagnetic. However, O₂ is experimentally found to be paramagnetic, a fact that requires molecular‑orbital theory for proper explanation. The other statements (A, C, D) are either consistent with or can be rationalised within the basic valence‑bond framework.
